items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia, le news. Helsinki: “Finlandia e Norvegia hanno sentito Putin sull’Ucraina”
items.summary: Scatta la tregua a Oleshky. Droni russi danneggiano ponte a Kiev
items.content:
Telefonate con il presidente finlandese Stubb e il primo ministro norvegese Store per il presidente russo Putin. Oggetto il possibile accordo di pace per l'Ucraina. Le conversazioni seguono la visita dell'inviato statunitense Witkoff a Putin , avvenuta la scorsa settimana in seguito a incontri con Zelensky e i leader dei paesi nordici a Oslo

Helsinki: “Finlandia e Norvegia hanno sentito Putin sull’Ucraina”

Cremlino: “Non smentiamo nè confermiamo la conversazione di Putin con Stubb e Store”

Il presidente russo Vladimir Putin ha avuto una conversazione telefonica con il presidente finlandese Alexander Stubb e il primo ministro norvegese Jonas Gahr Støre. Lo ha confermato all'agenzia Tass il portavoce del Cremlino Dmitry Peskov

Subito dopo aver parlato al telefono con il presidente russo Vladimir Putin, il presidente finlandese Alex SDtubb e il primo ministro norvegese Jonas Store hanno telefonato a Vladymyr Zelensky. Oggetto dei colloqui, il processo di pace per l'Ucraina e il prossimo trilaterale Russia-Ucraina-Usa in programma per novembre

Helsinki: “Finlandia e Norvegia hanno sentito Putin sull’Ucraina”

Il presidente finlandese Alexander Stubb e il primo ministro norvegese Jonas Gahr Stoere hanno avuto oggi una conversazione telefonica con il presidente russo Vladimir Putin in merito alla guerra in Ucraina, secondo quanto riferito in un comunicato dall’ufficio di Stubb. I leader dell’Europa occidentale hanno per lo più evitato ogni contatto con Putin da quando la Russia ha lanciato la sua guerra su vasta scala in Ucraina nel febbraio 2022. «La discussione è stata franca e sostanziale. Siamo paesi confinanti con la Russia. L’esito di questa guerra avrà un impatto diretto sulla nostra sicurezza e su quella dell’Europa in generale. Per porre fine alla guerra sono necessari colloqui diretti», ha affermato Stubb in una dichiarazione. La Russia ha spesso accusato i governi europei di alimentare la guerra armando l’Ucraina e rifiutandosi di dialogare con Mosca. Ha contrapposto la loro posizione a quella del presidente degli Stati Uniti Donald Trump, che ha intrattenuto contatti con Putin e ha cercato – finora senza successo – di mediare un accordo di pace. Stoere e Stubb hanno incontrato la scorsa settimana a Oslo l’inviato speciale statunitense Steve Witkoff e il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelenskiy, un giorno prima che Witkoff incontrasse Putin a San Pietroburgo. Il Cremlino ha dichiarato, al termine dei colloqui tra Putin e Witkoff, che la Russia era disposta a riprendere i colloqui di pace con l’Ucraina mediati dagli Stati Uniti a novembre, per la prima volta da febbraio.

Cremlino: “Non smentiamo nè confermiamo la conversazione di Putin con Stubb e Store”

"Non posso né confermare né smentire", ha commentato il portavoce presidenziale russo, Dmitry Peskov, la notizia diffusa da Bloomberg secondo cui il presidente Vladimir Putin potrebbe avere oggi una conversazione telefonica con il presidente finlandese Alexander Stubb e il primo ministro norvegese Jonas Gahr Store. Stubb e Store hanno partecipato a colloqui con la delegazione ucraina e l'inviato speciale di Donald Trump, Steve Witkoff, a Oslo la scorsa settimana. Witkoff ha poi incontrato Vladimir Putin a San Pietroburgo

Zelensky: “I russi hanno attaccato con 16 missili balistici e 280 droni”

La Russia ha attaccato la notte scorsa l'Ucraina con 16 missili balistici e 280 droni. Lo afferma sui social il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky. "In totale - ha affermato invocando gli alleati per l'invio di Patriot - stanotte sono stati lanciati 16 missili balistici. Più di 280 droni. Purtroppo ci sono state vittime, ci sono stati colpi a Kiev, in particolare sul Ponte Sud. Una grave escalation nell'operazione russa contro la nostra logistica. Ci sono stati attacchi anche a Kiev, Vinnytsia, Zaporizhia, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Odessa, Chernihiv, Sumy, Donetsk, Kherson e nella regione di Chernivtsi. Quasi ovunque, gli obiettivi russi sono le infrastrutture energetiche, logistiche e urbane ordinarie"

Kiev: “Chiuso il ponte sud della capitale dopo i raid notturni”

A causa dei raid notturni, il ponte sud della capitale è stato chiuso al traffico e sulla riva sinistra del fiume si sono verificati ingorghi enormi anche a causa del servizio limitato della metropolitana. Anche il servizio ferroviario sulla linea verde tra le stazioni di Osokorky e Chervonyi Khutir è stato temporaneamente sospeso. Lo riportano i media ucraini

Governatore russo: “Un morto e sei feriti per gli attacchi ucraini a Bryansk”

Una persona è rimasta uccisa e altre sei ferite in un attacco ucraino a Bryansk. Lo ha riferito il governatore della regione russa, Egor Kovalchuk. "Un uomo è morto nel distretto di Bezhitsky colpito da un tubo contenente esplosivo sganciato da un drone", ha scritto il governatore su Telegram. "Secondo informazioni preliminari, sei persone sono rimaste ferite nell'attacco con il drone nel distretto di Sovietsky", ha aggiunto Kovalchuk

Due persone sono rimaste uccise in seguito al raid russo effettuato nella notte sul quartiere di Novobavarskyi a Kharkiv. Lo ha reso noto su telegram il sindaco della città, Igor Terekhov. "Sono stati danneggiati palazzi residenziali, case private e automobil", ha spiegato. I feriti sono quattro fra cui una ragazza di 17 anni

È di un morto e 15 feriti il bilancio dei raid notturni russi su Kiev. Un comunicato del sindaco Vitaliy Klitschko , precisa che una donna di 46 anni è deceduta a seguito di un attacco nel distretto di Desnyanskyi. I raid hanno danneggiato “edifici residenziali pluripiano e privati, strutture sanitarie, una stazione della metropolitana, un dormitorio universitario, un centro commerciale, un edificio amministrativo, tram e automobili"”.

Un attacco russo ha danneggiato un importante ponte sul fiume Dnipro a Kiev. "È stato colpito il ponte Pivdennyi", ha scritto su Telegram il sindaco di Kiev, Vitaliy Klitschko. "Anche le infrastrutture della metropolitana presenti sul ponte hanno subito danni", ha aggiunto il primo cittadino. Il ponte si trova nella zona meridionale della capitale ucraina. I danni sono legati al lancio di numerosi missili balistici verso la capitale ucraina. Funzionari comunali hanno aggiunto che il servizio ferroviario sul ponte è stato sospeso.

È entrata in vigore la tregua tra Ucraina e Russia volta a consentire l'accesso degli aiuti umanitari alla città di Oleshky , occupata dalla Russia. L'annuncio era stato dato la scorsa settimana dalla first lady degli Stati Uniti Melania Trump . Entrambe le parti hanno dichiarato che avrebbero rispettato la tregua a partire dalle 3 del mattino, ora locale

I russi hanno lanciato attacchi questa notte a Kharkiv , uccidendo due persone. A confermarlo, il sindaco del distretto, Igor Terekhov , in un post su telegram ripreso da Ukrinform. Gli attacchi hanno danneggiato palazzi residenziali, case private e automobili.

items.title: Jannik Sinner: “Il corpo è l’unico avversario che non puoi battere. Se dice stop devi accettarlo”
items.summary: Il ragazzo che si definiva “programmato” ha dovuto riprogrammarsi. E cambiare formato alla sua esistenza. Lo rivedremo in campo al Six Kings Slam di Riad a fine anno, nel frattempo deve curare corpo e umore. Intanto ha letto, ha guardato la F1, ha partecipato alla fashion week e giocato alla Play. In questa intervista iniziata ad agosto e finita a ottobre, rievoca i momenti tristi e quelli più felici: “La differenza la fa sempre il lavoro, non la fortuna. Quella aiuta a vincere un punto, mai la partita”
items.content:
Il cappuccio c’è ancora, la camminata dinoccolata pure. Quattro anni fa diceva che fuori dal campo “il rumore si spegne, anzi non esiste più”. Quest’estate il rumore è arrivato da dentro: un ginocchio, il destro, ha detto no. Niente Canada, niente Cincinnati, niente New York, niente Asia, niente Atp Finals a Torino. L’ultimo Slam vincente è datato 12 luglio, sull’erba di Wimbledon , con il secondo titolo consecutivo ai Championships e Zverev battuto in finale. 47 partite giocate, solo 3 perse. Ha sconfitto tutti i migliori: da Alcaraz a Tiafoe, da Medvedev a Jódar. Poi il silenzio, interrotto da qualche video sui social, poche parole, sempre le stesse: non sono pronto. E alla fine: ci vediamo nel 2027.

Sinner è costretto a lasciare il trono, ma non è un’abdicazione, tornerà dopo l’autunno. È iscritto all’One Point Slam in programma il 13 gennaio nel corso dell’opening week degli Australian Open. Anche senza corona non rischia l’invisibilità. Fino a fine dicembre ogni torneo avrà un giocatore in più, quello che non c’è. Ritroveremo Jannik nelle domande delle conferenze stampa, nei pronostici, in una classifica che si muoverà senza di lui, perfino nei successi degli altri, costretti a convivere con una piccola nota a margine: mancava Sinner. L’assenza ha questo di particolare: non si consuma, cresce. Il ragazzo che si definiva “programmato” ha dovuto riprogrammarsi. E cambiare formato alla sua esistenza, non più a rettangolo. Il numero uno che misurava la vita in 23,77 metri per 10,97 ha scoperto che ci sono altre misure. Ma non ha cambiato idea su quale sia la sua. Quest’intervista è stata una lunga partita iniziata ad agosto e finita a ottobre all’atto dell’annuncio del suo stop.

Cosa resta di un’estate passata a guardare il tennis lontano della rete?

Ma non sarà che questo tennis rompe troppo i corpi? Una caviglia cede, una rotula si lussa, un polso non regge più migliaia di accelerazioni, un’anca si consuma dalle torsioni. Ormai non c’è torneo senza ritiri.

“Gli infortuni fanno parte dello sport, bisogna essere intelligenti e capire quanto e quando giocare. Serve avere una visione a lungo termine, non c’è solo l’oggi, si semina ora, ma il raccolto ha altri tempi. E la differenza la fa sempre il lavoro, la preparazione che fai, non la fortuna. Quella aiuta a vincere un punto, non la partita”.

La russa Kristina Liutova a luglio, a soli 16 anni, ha conquistato il WTA 250 di Memphis partendo dalle qualificazioni. C’è chi mette in guardia l’infanzia dall’orco che divora.

“Non faccio io le regole, ma perché togliere agli adolescenti una bella storia da raccontare? Hanno vissuto un’emozione forte, hanno combattuto, si sono impegnati. C’è un’età in cui lo sport ti dà la voce per essere ascoltato e diventa uno strumento per capire chi sei e crescere. Non puoi ancora essere grande nella società, in tanti altri settori ti viene rimproverato che non hai l’età giusta invece lo sport ti offre occasioni senza giudicarti o chiederti la carta d’identità. Guardate la stagione di Lamine Yamal, campione del mondo con la Spagna a 19 anni. Perché aver paura che troppa gioventù produca guasti? E se invece offrisse nuovi orizzonti e aiutasse a mettere in mostra qualità che ancora nessuno ha visto? Lasciateli giocare, i ragazzi. Kimi Antonelli ha esordito che non aveva ancora la patente e, a proposito, io quella per le moto sono finalmente riuscito a prenderla. Se uno si merita il successo non vedo problemi, così come hanno il diritto di stare in campo Messi e Cristiano Ronaldo, anche se non sono più teenager, senza dimenticare Djokovic”.

“Di tutto. Di come ci si relaziona con gli altri, delle persone che abbiamo attorno, di come fare in certe situazioni. Facciamo sport diversi, lui ha 20 anni, io 25, ma ci confrontiamo molto. Mi chiedono: scambieresti uno Slam con un successo in una gara di F1? Dai, inutile rispondere, è una cosa che non capiterà mai”.

Se potesse incontrare Jannik di 10 anni fa cosa gli direbbe?

“Quello che ho imparato: il talento senza lavoro non è niente. Devi fare scelte, valutarne le conseguenze, seguire la tua meta. Gli direi di vivere bene quei momenti, non ho rimorsi, non gli consiglierei di cambiare strada, ma di scegliere bene le persone di cui circondarsi. Non sono pentito, la mia famiglia c’è sempre stata, ho sempre potuto contare su un papà bravo anche in cucina”.

“È molto migliorata, non esce più durante i miei incontri, il rifiuto a sedere nel Royal Box a Wimbledon è perché non vuole essere osservata e scrutata dalle telecamere quando gioco. Non ha tutti i torti, non le piace la tensione, anche se ora riesce a essere più tranquilla”.

Cosa racconta di noi il tennis meglio o diversamente dagli altri sport? Perché riesce a essere così contemporaneo?

“Non lo so perché, bisognerebbe chiederlo a chi lo guarda, non a chi lo gioca. Forse fa esistere le diversità, le valorizza, la rivalità nasce dalla differenza, si vince e si perde, ognuno trova un suo motivo per identificarsi in chi gli somiglia o in chi vorrebbe essere. E questo lo rende affascinante”.

Ma il mondo rivuole in campo Sinner-Alcaraz. Non cerca altro.

“Non siamo tutti uguali, i contrasti esaltano. Magari io vengo vissuto come il campione disciplinato e ostinato e Carlos come quello mediterraneo e stravagante. Questa è la cosa bella, avere qualcuno che ti spinge al limite. E il tennis ha sempre vissuto di questo: da Borg-McEnroe a Sampras-Agassi fino a quando la rivalità a due è diventata a tre con Federer-Nadal-Djokovic”.

Gli eroi dello sport vanno più di moda degli attori. Una volta si sognava con il cinema, oggi alle sfilate ci siete voi.

“Ma non è una competizione, né siamo in contrapposizione. Il mondo del basket americano da tempo è attento alla moda e i suoi giocatori fuori dal campo ci tengono a mostrare la personalità anche con gli abiti. Nessuno sostituisce nessuno, credo sia solo una questione piattaforme diverse e di nuovi soggetti”.

Prima di lei nessuno entrava in campo con una borsa firmata. Ora la imitano.

“Con Gucci sento affinità. Mi piace essere un po’ diverso con cose normali, belle, eleganti. Così come amo essere a mio agio e questo marchio me lo permette. Non sono un tipo chiassoso, sono anche astemio, non sopporto il sapore dell’alcol, al massimo bevo un po’ di champagne o di vino bianco”.

Se potesse cancellare una giornata della sua vita, non riviverla più.

“Non sarebbe un momento sportivo, né la sconfitta in finale con Alcaraz a Parigi 2025, né in semifinale con Djokovic a Melbourne a inizio anno”.

“Vorrei cancellare ciò che ho provato il giorno in cui sono andato via di casa. Lo strazio di quando a 13 anni e mezzo, a Milano, ho salutato mio padre perché le nostre strade si separavano e un filo si spezzava. Ci stavamo lasciando, piangevo io per lo strappo, ma anche lui. Di quel giorno lì farei a meno, fu un’emozione troppo forte”.

“Forse a me lo ha fatto trovare, anche se ho sofferto. Mi ha fatto capire che fare una scelta significa ottenere cose nuove e perderne altre. Ci può essere dolore, ma anche la consapevolezza che quella decisione costata molto non va sprecata. Devi fare di tutto per servirla al meglio, senza rimpianti. Con impegno, costanza, lavoro”.

“La purezza di una domenica d’inverno con i miei amici a sciare sulle Dolomiti. La sensazione di una bella giornata facendo una cosa che ti piace. Un gruppo di ragazzi che vuole divertirsi. Ci metterei anche un qualsiasi momento con la mia famiglia e uno sui go-kart dalle parti di Cuneo con il pilota Antonio Giovinazzi e il ciclista Giulio Ciccone. A me la velocità piace, non è un mistero. Ho bisogno dell’adrenalina, di tenere lontana la noia”.

Ha 25 anni, se potesse scegliere che età avere oggi, cambierebbe?

“Va bene così. Tengo tutto: le persone, le esperienze, gli incontri fatti”.

“Non ci penso proprio. So che Serena Williams, Sharapova, Agassi, McEnroe, Nadal, Borg l’hanno scritta. Ma io sono ancora giovane, preferisco i colpi alle parole, magari ne riparliamo tra 20 anni. Voglio durare, avere una carriera lunga. Ora mi sono dovuto fermare e alzare la testa oltre le righe, ma voglio riabbassarla sulla palla. So che fuori c’è dell’altro, ma il mio è lì. In quel rettangolo che si chiama tennis”.

PROFILO Jannik Sinner (2001) è stato nel 2024 il primo tennista italiano alla testa del ranking mondiale, dopo aver vinto Australian e US Open. Nel ’25 si conferma a Melbourne e conquista Wimbledon. Il ’26 è da record: 5 Masters 1000 e di nuovo Wimbledon. Poi si ferma e a ottobre annuncia lo stop. Ora il suo obiettivo è tornare nel ’27.

Paolo Roversi (1947) è uno dei fotografi italiani di moda più noti a livello internazionale. Ha collaborato con i principali magazine e i più grandi brand. Originario di Ravenna, dal 1981 lavora nel suo studio di rue Paul Fort, a Parigi.

items.title: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model (155 responses)
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.cloudflare.com/kv-cache-exposure-remediation/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50252159 Points: 137 # Comments: 45
items.content:
On September 8, 2026, we were alerted by a security researcher, Gadi Evron from Knostic , to a tenant isolation issue affecting the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model ( @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3 ) starting on August 27, 2026. We have remediated the issue, and we restored the model on September 9. We have confirmed that no other model hosted on Workers AI was affected.

Between August 27 and September 9, a small number of customers using the GLM 5.3 Workers AI model received responses that contained data from other customers' requests made to the same model shortly before theirs. In total, 155 responses were affected, all to prompts longer than 681,280 tokens.

After excluding our own testing and the researcher's, the requests we identified are consistent in timing and volume with ordinary long-context use, not with someone repeatedly exploiting the bug. We found no evidence of deliberate exploitation.

Today we are publishing this report alongside a post from SGLang, the open-source inference engine that we use, as a coordinated disclosure. This post describes the bug that caused this issue, our response timeline, and the subsequent hardening we have conducted on our production SGLang deployments. We also detail our continued efforts with the upstream maintainers of SGLang to address this and similar bugs.

GLM is a text generation model from Z.ai that is built for agentic coding workflows; it is one of the many models available through Workers AI. Gadi Evron submitted a report on September 8 through our HackerOne program stating that very long prompts sent to @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3 on Workers AI sometimes returned text that belonged to other users' sessions. Cloudflare reproduced the issue the next morning and took the model offline within 40 minutes of declaring an incident. We then deployed a corrected configuration and a patched inference engine, and restored service the same day.

This specific report of cross-request KV cache exposure was the result of two overlapping issues. The first was a misconfiguration of the open-source inference engine, SGLang, used by Cloudflare. We deployed GLM 5.3 with a 1,048,576-token context window, but the KV cache pool on our prefill GPUs only had room for 681,280 tokens. We were aware of this mismatch before launch. We expected the engine to return an error for any prompt it could not process, and our long-context tests returned successful responses, so we did not believe this to be an issue.

The second was a bug in how SGLang handled the resulting over-length requests in disaggregated prefill/decode mode. A prompt that did not fit the pool was internally marked as rejected and replaced with a one-token placeholder, but instead of aborting the request and returning a client error, prefill generated the KV cache for the placeholder prompt and transferred it to the decode node. The decode node received a "transfer complete" message and assumed that prefill overwrote the KV cache from previous requests with the full prompt for this request, when in fact it left the majority of the previous state intact. The decode node subsequently generated a response while attending over stale cache pages that still held data from earlier requests. As a result, responses to prompts longer than 681,280 tokens could contain data from other users' GLM 5.3 sessions.

After disabling the model , we took the following actions to correct this vulnerability before restoring public access to it:

To fix our configuration, we made the pool hold the full context. We adjusted our GLM 5.3 configuration to match our GLM 5.2 configuration, which freed enough GPU memory that the prefill KV pool now holds about 2.04 million tokens, roughly twice the 1,048,576-token context length. A prompt that fits the context window now always fits the pool, so the rejection path is never reached for a valid request. This alone prevents the bug from being exercised.

To fix the engine, we also made the rejection path safe. Relying on pool size alone is fragile: any change to quantization, tensor parallelism, CUDA graph sizes, or a future model version changes the pool size in a way that's easy to miss. Furthermore, there may be other situations in which the prefill scheduler can reject a request and trigger the same bug. To prevent this, we also patched the engine so that a request carrying a pending rejection is retired at the disaggregation admission queue, with its original error, before any bootstrap, allocation, or KV transfer happens. We proposed this upstream as #38704 , which also had the decode node verify that the number of tokens transferred matches the number it reserved. The fix was already on SGLang main in #36988 , merged September 6 for a related failure path but not yet released. The maintainers also merged #38935 , which rejects these requests earlier, following our approach.

We validated both changes against the researcher's reproduction script and our own canary-marker tests before restoring the model.

Workers AI runs GLM 5.3 with SGLang in a disaggregated configuration: a pool of prefill GPUs processes the prompt and produces the model's KV cache for it, then hands that cache over remote direct memory access (RDMA), via Mooncake , to a pool of decode GPUs that generate the response. We have written about this architecture before in our posts on high-performance LLMs and smaller, faster, safer models .

The KV cache in GPU memory is a shared pool of fixed-size pages. Each request is assigned pages when it is admitted and releases them when it finishes. Pages are not currently zeroed between requests; the next request that gets a page simply overwrites it. This approach is common among inference engines and is necessary to achieve the best performance, but it means that the inference engine is responsible for tracking ownership of these memory pages. KV cache page ownership and lifetime tracking has to deal with not just shared ownership within a node (KV cache offload and token generation both access the memory with different lifetimes), but also ownership that is technically shared with the remote prefill node (which holds a simultaneous mutable reference to the page).

Furthermore, the size of this pool is not a configuration value. SGLang sizes it at startup from whatever GPU memory remains after loading the model weights. The model's advertised context length is a separate configuration value. Nothing forces the two to agree, and it is our job to check that they do.

On our GLM 5.3 prefill nodes with our configuration, the pool came to 681,280 tokens while the model's context length is 1,048,576 tokens. The selected KV pool size is printed by SGLang in logs during startup and exposed as a metric. We were aware of this size mismatch; however, during pre-launch testing we observed successful HTTP status codes and a streaming body with no error frames during benchmarking. We assumed that the engine was capable of gracefully handling the difference between the KV cache pool and requested context window via streaming or some other mechanism.

This was one critical gap in our testing: we only validated HTTP response codes and engine performance at long contexts, without validating model output and coherence. We now check KV pool size against context length directly, from the running engine, before any disaggregated deployment change ships, rather than inferring it from response codes.

In v0.5.21, the SGLang team has now addressed this bug in how it was handling prompts longer than the KV pool size. Here’s what was happening before.

When a prompt arrived that was longer than the KV pool could hold, SGLang's scheduler rejected it. The rejection path ( Req.set_finish_with_abort ) recorded the error to be returned to the client and swapped the prompt for a one-token placeholder so that the request could drain through the normal batch machinery without allocating real memory. On a single-node deployment this worked: the placeholder ran, the batch finished, and the client received an error.

In disaggregated mode such as we operate, the admission queues on both prefill and decode checked whether a request was finished , not whether it was rejected . A rejected request reported itself as live. So:

Every request over the threshold behaved this way. This bug had been reported to SGLang by another user as issue #30233 on July 6, 2026, which Cloudflare noticed while investigating this incident. We had been flagging these types of issues with SGLang since v0.5.10 and this security incident sped up work that Cloudflare had already started in collaboration with the SGLang team. The patch for this issue was released in SGLang v0.5.20, with follow-ups in v0.5.21 and v0.5.22, and is available for all other operators dependent on SGLang to use. We highly recommend all operators update SGLang dependencies to v0.5.22 or later. For more details on specific PRs, read on below.

GLM 5.3 was the only model affected by this bug. Every other disaggregated deployment on Workers AI has KV pools larger than its context length on both prefill and decode, so no request could reach the rejection path. We have applied the engine fix and the hardening described below to every model we serve with SGLang, and our deployment checks require them for every new deployment.

items.title: 'Maxxing' selected as Dictionary.com word of the year
items.summary: "Whatever we're doing, we want to push it further," said an expert on why Americans are embracing the term, which is short for maximising.
items.content:
Americans have gone all in on "maxxing", making it the 2026 Word of the Year for Dictionary.com.

Short for maximising, the term "can be used on its own or added to the end of any word to convey you're doing something to the fullest or optimizing it as much as possible", Dictionary.com said in a statement.

It's a major departure from two years ago, when the site, after analysing US social media trends, news stories, and search data, chose demure as word of the year. Last year's was "67".

"Maxxing is the linguistic manifestation of a culture increasingly preoccupied with getting the most out of everything," said Steve Johnson, director of lexicography for the Dictionary Media Group.

Digital media used "maxxing" nearly 19 times more in August 2026 compared to the 2025 monthly average, Dictionary.com found. The site also considered affordability, data centre, odyssey, and the shortened form of uncle, "unc", as potential words of the year.

On social media, many people in Generation Z and younger - those under 30 - post extensively about their maxxing efforts to achieve all sorts of perfection.

Influencers focused on fitness and wellness post about "proteinmaxxing" and "fibermaxxing". Those giving their full attention to improving sleep habits say they are "sleepmaxxing".

The influencer Clavicular has gained thousands of followers as he chronicles his extreme "looksmaxxing" - working to meet a set of prescribed criteria for attractiveness, with particular importance given to jawlines, eyes and physique.

"Whatever we're doing, we want to push it further," Johnson said. "But its expanding uses also reveal how people are responding to that impulse. Some embrace it. Some exaggerate it for laughs. Others subvert it entirely to describe stepping back from the relentless pursuit of more."

People were playing with the term - and idea - for decades before Clavicular started posting videos.

In the opening song for the 1990s television show The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, for example, Will Smith raps: "Chillin' out, maxin', relaxin' all cool."

"Unfortunately, by the time the dictionary gets a hold of it, that probably means that it's reached critical mass," says teacher Lauren Cella.

Cella, a content creator known for her viral Gen Z history lessons, says she and her students have been using "maxxing" for some time as a suffix.

"They're actually, in their own way, reinventing grammar, which I think is super cool," she says.

Maxxing gives the students permission to "optimise to meet a goal" or do something others might think of as "cringe", and allows them to own it, she says.

"It's a fun, harmless way that kids are expressing themselves and sharing different goals that they have," she says.

Linguist Vanessa Croft, who teaches English, says the internet and digital media make language move at "warp speed", even faster than radio, film or television ever did. As swiftly as new terms are added to the lexicon, they can just as quickly fall out of favour.

"By the time millennials and Gen X or Gen Y start using the terms, Gen Z and Gen Alpha aren't using those terms anymore," she says.

While she and her secondary-school aged students are still "maxxing" too, they are now using it "almost ironically", she says.

items.title: Trump administration illegally fired James Comey's daughter, judge rules
items.summary: Maurene Comey believes she was let go from her job as a federal prosecutor because her father is the former FBI director.
items.content:
The US justice department illegally fired Maurene Comey, the daughter of former Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) director James Comey, a federal judge has ruled.

Comey, who lost her job as a federal prosecutor in New York in July 2025, sued the government, arguing she was unlawfully fired because of her father, a critic of US President Donald Trump, and because of her perceived political affiliations.

Judge Jesse Furman ruled on Monday that the Trump administration must reinstate her and that she must be given back pay.

A spokesperson for the justice department said in a statement that it disagreed with the decision and "will appeal in due course".

In his ruling, Judge Furman said Comey's dismissal violated the US Constitution as well as her right to a fair legal process.

He said the US attorney general can fire federal prosecutors but only "in a particular manner and only for certain reasons".

Furman noted that in Comey's role, "she was assigned some of the country's highest profile cases and consistently received the highest accolades from supervisors and peers alike".

Comey has worked on cases against the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, his accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell, and hip-hop mogul Sean "Diddy" Combs, who was convicted on prostitution-related charges involving his two ex-girlfriends last year.

Furman ordered that Comey be given back pay from July until December 2025, when she accepted a new job.

In a statement, Comey's lawyers said: "This hard-earned victory belongs to Ms Comey, to all civil servants, and to all fighting for the rule of law."

Comey had previously said the only reason she was told about her firing was that it "came from Washington".

A complaint filed by her lawyers in September 2025 stated that they believed Comey had been fired "solely or substantially because her father is former FBI Director James B Comey, or because of her perceived political affiliation and beliefs, or both".

The justice department said in court filings that the decision was made by former Attorney General Pam Bondi.

The Trump administration has twice brought charges against James Comey, including for allegedly lying to Congress, but that case was dismissed by a judge who said the prosecutor who brought the case was unlawfully appointed.

Earlier this year, the justice department charged Comey with knowingly and wilfully making a threat to take the life of, and to inflict bodily harm, on the president. He has denied any wrongdoing.

The case stems from a 2025 Instagram post shared by Comey that contained a photo of seashells on a beach arranged to read "86 47".

"Eighty-six" is a slang term for "get rid of", and prosecutors allege it encourages violence against Trump.

Comey surrenders over charge of threatening Trump's life in Instagram post

Prosecutor in Diddy and Epstein cases fired by US justice department

items.title: Pope's South American trip to go ahead as planned after lung cancer surgery
items.summary: The Pope underwent surgery in to remove a tumour on the lower part of his right lung and is gradually resuming his duties.
items.content:
The Vatican has confirmed that Pope Leo will go on his South American tour as planned, following his surgery for lung cancer.

He was diagnosed with lung cancer and underwent successful surgery in Rome on 13 October to remove a tumour on the lower part of his right lung.

The 71-year-old is scheduled to travel to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on 6-17 November, the Vatican said, adding that the he was looking forward to it "with great joy and enthusiasm".

The Pope will follow the same programme as planned, visiting 10 cities on the tour.

"I am looking forward to returning to the continent where I've experienced so many moments of my life," Pope Leo said.

The Pope's trip will begin in Uruguay on 8 November, where he will visit the capital Montevideo, as well as other key cities.

He will then travel to Argentina from November 11-17, visiting a number of places including the capital Buenos Aires.

After that he will spend six days in Peru, where roughly 76% of the population are Catholic, and will include stops in Lima, Chiclayo, Cuzco and Pucallpa.

Peru's Cardinal Castillo, the Archbishop of Lima, has said the trip would involve young people, women who help run community kitchens and members of the country's indigenous communities, according to Vatican News.

The archbishop highlighted the Pope's close ties with the people of Chiclayo, where he lived for several years. The Pope has Peruvian citizenship.

The Catholic Church sent him to Peru as a missionary in 1985 , when he was 30 years old.

He joined the Augustinian mission in Chulucanas, in the Peruvian department of Piura, and the following year, joined the mission in the city of Trujillo.

For almost three decades, he worked between the US and Peru.

Leo announced the news of his lung operation himself to the world on 11 October during his weekly Sunday prayers, telling the crowd in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a nodule on his lung.

He reassured pilgrims that the growth was "well-contained" and caught "at an early stage" but that his doctors had advised him to have it removed.

The surgery lasted for 90 minutes, and he was discharged from Rome's Gemelli hospital on 17 October.

The Pope's surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, said he was in an "absolutely satisfactory clinical condition", and said there were "no clinical reasons" why the trip should not go ahead.

Since his operation, the pope has been resting and gradually resuming his work. He has been "adjusting his daily schedule in consultation with his doctors to prioritise his recovery while continuing to fulfill the responsibilities of his ministry," the Vatican said.

Leo was "deeply grateful for the prayers and affection he has received from throughout the world," the Vatican said.

The Vatican said Friday that Leo would cancel a planned trip to Assisi on October 27th, on the recommendation of his doctors.

Pope Leo XIV thanks wellwishers in first event after cancer surgery

Pope discharged from hospital days after lung cancer surgery

items.title: Gli eredi di Elvis Presley contro Anthropic, 'ha usato 274 canzoni per addestrare IA'
items.summary: Chiedono 41 milioni di dollari di danni al colosso tecnologico
items.content: Battaglia legale degli eredi di Elvis Presley contro Anthropic: accusano il colosso dell'intelligenza artificiale di aver addestrato i suoi modelli di IA su centinaia di brani del leggendario artista senza alcuna autorizzazione. La nuova causa, depositata il 23 ottobre e di cui ha dato notizia la rivista Billboard, sostiene che Anthropic abbia violato il copyright di 274 canzoni della leggenda del rock, inclusi popolari successi come Can't Help Falling in Love, A Little Less Conversation e Don't Be Cruel. Chiedono più di 41 milioni di dollari di danni. "I querelanti legati a Elvis vogliono far valere diritti esclusivi nei confronti di un convenuto che ha costruito l'intero modello di business sulla violazione del copyright su una scala mai vista prima - scrive Richard Busch, l'avvocato principale che segue la causa -. I querelanti tengono moltissimo a proteggere queste canzoni iconiche". La causa è stata intentata da una divisione di Authentic Brands Group, il colosso delle licenze che detiene la maggior parte dei diritti di proprietà intellettuale relativi a Elvis Presley tra cui gran parte del suo catalogo musicale, i marchi commerciali a lui legati e i diritti sul suo nome e immagine. Al pari di altre aziende che operano nel campo dell'intelligenza artificiale, Anthropic sta già affrontando altre cause giudiziarie riguardanti il processo di addestramento dei propri modelli. Le società di IA - sottolinea Billboard - sostengono che tale processo sia tutelato dalla dottrina del fair use, uso legittimo, prevista dal diritto d'autore. Tuttavia la questione resta ancora aperta in decine di procedimenti legali, con in gioco potenziali risarcimenti per miliardi di dollari. Fino ad ora il contenzioso relativo alla musica generata dall'intelligenza artificiale si è concentrato principalmente su Suno, il principale generatore di brani basato sull'IA che nel 2024 è stato citato in giudizio dalle maggiori etichette discografiche. Ha raggiunto un accordo con Warner Music Group l'anno scorso e ha dichiarato di voler collaborare con l'industria musicale, ma deve ancora affrontare un acceso contenzioso legale con Umg e Sony Music.

items.title: Papa Leone andrà in Sudamerica: 'Felice di tornare dove ho vissuto'
items.summary: Confermato il viaggio tra Uruguay Argentina e Perù. I medici: 'Nessuna controindicazione'
items.content:
Papa Leone tira dritto. A meno di dieci giorni dalle sue dimissioni dal policlinico Agostino Gemelli, e dopo che già era arrivato il nulla osta ai viaggi aerei da parte del chirurgo che lo ha operato, il professore Stefano Margaritora, la Sala stampa della Santa Sede conferma ufficialmente il previsto viaggio di papa Leone in Uruguay, Argentina e Perù dal 6 al 17 novembre. Il viaggio apostolico si svolgerà "secondo programma": "il dottor Luigi Carbone conferma che il recupero postoperatorio del Santo Padre continua a progredire e gli ultimi esami medici confermano la buona salute", "non si ravvisano controindicazioni, visto il quadro clinico attuale, gli esami strumentali e di laboratorio eseguiti, che impediscano di intraprendere il prossimo viaggio apostolico", afferma il comunicato vaticano.

Niente modifiche quindi o variazioni di sorta che pure erano state ipotizzate trattandosi di un programma altamente impegnativo, con numerosi spostamenti sia in aereo, sia in elicottero per 6mila chilometri complessivi e toccando altezze vertiginose in particolare con la meta peruviana di Cuzco situata a 3 più di mila metri. "Sono felice di poter tornare nel continente nel quale ho vissuto tanti momenti della mia vita - dice lo stesso Prevost che è stato per molti anni missionario e quindi vescovo in Perù - . Possa questo viaggio essere un'occasione per aprire i nostri cuori gli uni agli altri, rafforzare la nostra comunione come fratelli e sorelle e rinnovare il nostro impegno ad annunciare il Vangelo con gioia!".

"Il Papa - si legge pure nel lungo comunicato - segue le raccomandazioni mediche con scrupolo e attenzione, e profonda determinazione nel continuare a servire la Chiesa, attende con grande gioia ed entusiasmo questo viaggio, che offrirà l'opportunità di rafforzare i legami di comunione con le Chiese locali, incoraggiare i fedeli nella loro missione e portare un messaggio di fede, speranza e pace". "Come già riferito - si precisa anche -, l'intervento chirurgico si è svolto con successo e senza complicazioni. I successivi accertamenti medici hanno confermato che la patologia era localizzata e che non sono necessari ulteriori trattamenti oncologici". Sempre la nota vaticana, riavvolge il nastro dall'uscita dal Gemelli: "Dal suo rientro in Vaticano, il Papa ha ripreso gradualmente le proprie attività, adattando il programma quotidiano in accordo con i medici per dare priorità al recupero postoperatorio, continuando al tempo stesso ad assolvere le responsabilità del suo ministero. Ha mantenuto importanti appuntamenti e impegni pubblici, prestando attenzione alle esigenze di ogni giornata e riservando adeguati momenti di riposo".

Leone che salterà domani la tappa mai ufficialmente annunciata dal Vaticano di Assisi dove avrebbe dovuto prendere parte all'incontro interreligioso promosso dalla Comunità di Sant'Egidio a 40 anni da quello svoltosi per impulso di san Giovanni Paolo II dove manderà invece un videomessaggio, conferma così indirettamente che priorità del suo pontificato è cercare un dialogo tra Nord e Sud del mondo, lui che è americano di nascita ma anche cittadino del Sud di adozione.

items.title: Type Server Protocol
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/microsoft/pylance-release/blob/main/docs/tsp/type-server-protocol.md Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50248371 Points: 243 # Comments: 163
items.content:
The Type Server Protocol (TSP) is a JSON-RPC protocol for asking a type server for Python analysis data. A type server maintains the type-analysis state for a workspace and answers requests for the protocol version, snapshots, Python search paths, import resolution, and type queries (computed, declared, and expected types).

The protocol uses Language Server Protocol (LSP) data shapes and conventions where they are useful, such as Position and Range , and it represents URIs as strings the same way LSP does. TSP methods use the typeServer/ prefix.

The protocol artifacts in this folder are the authoritative definitions:

TSP uses semantic version strings for client/server compatibility checks. While the protocol is in the 0.x line, minor version changes may be breaking. Patch version changes remain backward compatible within the same minor line.

A client starts a type server and communicates with it over the main JSON-RPC connection using a transport the server supports, such as stdio or Node IPC. When using stdio, stdout must be reserved for JSON-RPC protocol messages.

A type server is expected to receive enough workspace and document state to answer the TSP requests it supports. Clients commonly use normal LSP initialization and document synchronization for this state, then send typeServer/* requests on the same JSON-RPC connection.

TSP also supports optional extra read-only connections. The original connection remains the main connection and owns initialization, workspace state, document synchronization, state-changing notifications, and connection control. Extra connections are opened only after client and server negotiate support during initialization.

Multi-connection mode is an optional performance feature. It lets a client open additional local channels to the same type server for read-only TSP requests, while the main connection continues to own the mutable workspace state.

Clients should use multi-connection mode only when they can benefit from concurrent read-only work, such as high-volume type queries or background workers that should not block the main JSON-RPC connection. A server must still work correctly in single-connection mode. Multi-connection support must not be required for protocol correctness.

Multi-connection support is negotiated through the normal LSP initialize request and response. A client that can open extra TSP channels advertises the supported transport kinds under capabilities.experimental.typeServerMultiConnection :

A server that can serve extra TSP channels returns the same capability shape in the initialize result:

Multi-connection mode is enabled only when both sides advertise typeServerMultiConnection and the two supportedTransports lists have at least one transport in common. If either side omits the capability, or if there is no common transport, the session remains single-connection and the client must not send typeServer/connection .

The currently supported built-in transport kind for extra connections is ipc . This negotiation is separate from the main connection, which can use stdio or Node IPC.

After initialization and transport negotiation, the client opens an extra channel by sending typeServer/connection on the main connection:

For ipc , the args array identifies the endpoint or endpoints that the server should connect to. The server should validate the request, connect to the supplied endpoint promptly, and return a result with success: true when it accepts the request. If the server cannot open the channel, it should return success: false and include a short message when useful for logs.

An ipc endpoint is expected to provide a full-duplex JSON-RPC stream when the platform IPC mechanism supports it. In that case, args contains one endpoint string:

If the platform IPC mechanism exposes only one-way endpoints, args contains two endpoint strings. The endpoint names are from the type server's perspective: the first endpoint is the server input stream, and the second endpoint is the server output stream.

The client closes an extra channel by sending typeServer/connection on the main connection with the same transport kind and endpoint identity:

The server should stop serving the matching extra channel and close the transport promptly. A client may also tear down its local transport if the server does not complete the close within the client's timeout budget.

The close request should use the same args shape that opened the channel: one endpoint for a full-duplex IPC stream, or the same input/output endpoint pair for a split IPC stream.

The main connection owns all state-changing traffic. The following must remain main-connection-only:

Extra connections are TSP-only and read-only. They may be used for requests that do not mutate server state and whose results are valid for the snapshot supplied by the client.

The allowed TSP messages on an extra connection are bound to the negotiated TSP version. If a server reports support for a TSP version and advertises multi-connection support for that session, it must support every extra-connection TSP message defined for that version.

The table below lists the TSP version that first allows each message on an extra connection:

Servers should reject LSP traffic, state-changing notifications, typeServer/connection , and any TSP message not allowed for the negotiated TSP version when received on an extra connection.

A snapshot is a non-negative integer that identifies a point-in-time view of the type server's analysis state. Type handles, declarations, symbols, and other returned objects are valid only for the snapshot in which they were returned unless a request explicitly says otherwise.

The type server must advance the snapshot whenever a previously returned type-analysis result may be invalid. Typical invalidating events include opened-file changes, closed files, configuration changes, watched-file changes, dependency changes, or any cache reset that changes analysis results.

If a type server stores source locations in another encoding, it must convert locations at the protocol boundary. Incorrect conversion can cause the client to request information for the wrong syntax node.

The type-query requests ( typeServer/getComputedType , typeServer/getDeclaredType , typeServer/getExpectedType ) identify a source construct with an arg that is either a node or a declaration. A node is a URI plus a source range. A declaration describes where and how a symbol is defined and is either a regular declaration, which is backed by a source AST node, or a synthesized declaration, which is created by the type checker and has no source node.

InvalidHandle is -1 and represents an invalid or unavailable handle. Clients and servers should treat it as a sentinel value, not as a valid object identifier.

Type results are JSON-serializable tagged objects. Each type includes a discriminator that tells the client how to interpret the rest of the object. The protocol supports built-in types, declared types, functions, classes, unions, modules, type variables, overload sets, synthesized types, and type references.

Every type object carries a numeric kind discriminator, a numeric id , and a bitfield of flags :

Type objects are snapshot-bound, and type IDs are response-local:

The current protocol is intentionally small. The exact parameters and result shapes are defined in the protocol artifacts; the table below lists every TSP message with its direction and payload shape.

A type server should implement the messages required by the client it integrates with and return undefined only where the protocol's result type allows it.

The three type-query requests differ by which type they report for the same node or declaration:

Errors should include enough message detail for a client log to identify the failed request, but they should not expose local secrets or implementation-only state.

items.title: Musk sfida Nolan e pubblica il primo corto sull'Odissea generato dall'IA Grok
items.summary: Il video è di sette minuti, è la prima puntata di una serie
items.content: L'assistente di intelligenza artificiale di X, Grok, ha pubblicato sul social un cortometraggio di sette minuti dedicato all'Odissea. Si tratta della prima puntata di una serie. Tre mesi fa, Elon Musk, proprietario di X, aveva annunciato una trasposizione cinematografica integrale, interamente generata tramite intelligenza artificiale e fedele al contesto storico. Il progetto è stato sviluppato in collaborazione con Wonder Studios e con il regista Dev Walker e si inserisce nella contesa a distanza tra Musk e Christopher Nolan. Nei mesi scorsi l'imprenditore aveva criticato apertamente la versione cinematografica dell'Odissea diretta da Nolan, contestando la presenza di interpreti non caucasici e transgender nel cast. Lo scontro riflette due antipodi: Musk promuove la creazione di contenuti automatizzati attraverso l'IA, mentre Nolan si è sempre definito scettico verso questa tecnologia. Il film del regista britannico, girato in sei Paesi con un cast imponente, è considerato tra i favoriti per i prossimi premi Oscar. Sul piano tecnico, il filmato di Grok mostra un certo passo in avanti rispetto ai precedenti esperimenti, con scene marine e volti che in diversi passaggi raggiungono una buona verosimiglianza visiva. Emergono tuttavia dei compromessi, con i limiti principali che riguardano la componente drammatica e la tenuta narrativa, frammentata tra lunghe spiegazioni parlate e brevi scambi di battute.

items.title: Oldest GUI application that still runs on Windows 11
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.enlyth.com/posts/oldest-windows-gui-app-win-11/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50248055 Points: 431 # Comments: 249
items.content:
For a while I’ve been wondering about a silly question, which is, what’s the oldest application with a GUI that will still run on Windows 11 without modifications or emulation.

Given Windows’ excellent backwards compatibility, I expected the answer to be something impressively old.

Sadly, Windows 11 can’t run 16-bit Windows programs by itself, because 64-bit Windows has no NTVDM , so we’re going to have to find something from the early NT era.

I remember asking this question a while ago on an anonymous forum, where someone pointed me to Win32s , and suggested to find an early release version of it with FREECELL.exe .

So I did exactly that, and lo and behold, FREECELL.EXE with a date modified of 22-Feb-93 running and fully playable, without any changes on the latest version of Windows 11:

At the time of this post, that’s a 33 years and 8 months old application, which is impressively almost as old as me.

So I kinda thought “cool”, considered this a solved mystery and forgot about it shortly afterwards. But for some reason, this question popped into my mind again lately and this time I decided to dig deeper to see if I can find something older.

Digging through old Windows versions on the Internet Archive, I found some early NT 3.1 pre-release versions that seemed promising, but the main issue seemed to be either incompatibility with today’s executable format or API changes that came later in development.

The earliest 1991 versions used a draft PE format not compatible with modern Windows, and builds up to mid-1992 assumed the cdecl calling convention instead of stdcall for Windows API calls, so arguments would get removed twice, as such:

There was one application that caught my eye though, from Build 347, and that was CDPLAYER.EXE , linked on 16-Nov-1992 . By then the calling convention was fixed, but the other programs in that build crash in their bundled C runtime. CDPLAYER.EXE avoids that by using the system’s crtdll.dll , and Windows 11 still ships a crtdll.dll in SysWOW64 .

That is because, duh, my computer doesn’t have a CD-ROM drive. But you can use a small DLL ( cdemu.dll ) to emulate one with some fake audio data and actually get it to play audio:

So earlier I mentioned that 16-bit programs are out of the picture because they are no longer supported.

But if you want, you can use something like otvdm to run older Windows applications.

Behold, a fully playable version of REVERSI.EXE dated 15-Nov-1985 running on Windows 11, taken from Windows 1.01:

And although using otvdm does feel like cheating, I thought it was cool enough to include in this post.

items.title: A Man from the Future: Why Johnny Can't Stop Abstracting
items.summary: Article URL: http://muratbuffalo.blogspot.com/2026/10/the-man-from-future-why-johnny-cant.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50247928 Points: 177 # Comments: 81
items.content:
I have come to suspect that to most people thinking is painful. Some of us are addicted to thinking. Some of us find it a necessity. Johnny enjoyed it. I even have the suspicion that he enjoyed almost nothing else.

I listened to Ananyo Bhattacharya's " The Man from the Future: The Visionary Life of John von Neumann " in my car during the many commute hours Bay Area traffic afforded me. I thought I should share the Johnny phenomena here.

I knew about von Neumann being a very influential mathematician/scientist/engineer but the full list still left me bedazzled. In his 53 years of life (1903-1957), von Neumann seeded so many fields. Every time there was an important discovery in physics, mathematics or computation, John von Neumann was there. Set theory and the foundations of mathematics. The mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics. Operator algebras (still called von Neumann algebras). Ergodic theory. Game theory. Expected utility theory (which is the foundation of most of modern mathematical economics). The Monte Carlo method. The stored-program computer architecture that every machine you have ever touched is built on. Numerical weather prediction. Fault-tolerant computing. Self-reproducing automata (cellular automata), and arguably, the logical structure of molecular biology, four years before Watson and Crick. There is also, unfortunately, the implosion lens for the Nagasaki bomb, and a decade of hawkish nuclear strategy.

At six, Janos (the OG hungarian name for Johnny) could divide eight-digit numbers in his head and hold a conversation in ancient Greek. He later added Latin, French, German, English, and Yiddish. The rumor was that he remembered everything he ever read. Many years later Herman Goldstine decided to test this by asking him to recite "A Tale of Two Cities." Von Neumann started on chapter one and had to be asked to stop fifteen minutes later.

Budapest around 1900 produced an absurd cluster of minds: von Neumann, Eugene Wigner, Edward Teller, Leo Szilard, Paul Erdős, Theodore von Kármán, George Pólya. When several of them turned up at Los Alamos and realized they had gone to high school together, Szilard joked that Hungary was a cover story for a Martian landing. But even inside the Martian cluster , von Neumann was the outlier. Wigner, a Nobel laureate himself, was asked at Los Alamos to explain the Hungarian phenomenon and said there is only one phenomenon that is worthy of explanation, and that phenomenon is John von Neumann. The cluster may be less mysterious than it looks: Budapest was one of the few genuinely welcoming places in Europe for Jewish families, and it pushed them toward the professions the nobility considered beneath them, mathematics among them. The schools then did the rest, with a nationwide math competition and top quality high school teachers.

As for the Johnny phenomenon, from the pedagogical perspective, the following stood out to me from Johnny's early years. The first is the dinner table. Von Neumann's father Miksa (Max), a lawyer turned banker so successful that the Emperor ennobled him for service to the national economy, ran the evening meal as a seminar. He would start by going through his own day: the cases he argued, the deals he negotiated, whatever was on his mind. Then each of the three boys would present on what they had been reading. The whole family would then argue about Heine's poetry, or antisemitism in Europe, or the paradoxes of omnipotence. Sometimes Max would bring home business clients, and the boys were allowed to grill them about whatever they wanted funded. Frequent guests included the director of Budapest's Theoretical Physics Institute and one of Freud's students.

The second is the languages. Max knew the good times could end, told his sons so explicitly, and wanted them able to survive anywhere in any language. He was preparing them to flee. He was right. When John was fifteen, the communists took over Hungary and targeted rich families like his. A few months later the counterrevolutionaries beat the communists and then massacred thousands of Jews for supposedly collaborating. The von Neumanns survived by leaving the country at the right moments, and possibly by being too rich.

Johnny's first ten years included no formal schooling at all, because organized primary schools were not a tradition there yet. He had governesses, private teachers, and his father's enormous library, and he apparently used it to memorize a 44-volume German history of the world, which he would later deploy to freak people out at parties.

Finally, when he did get to the Fasori Gymnasium at eleven, the math teacher, László Rátz, concluded fairly quickly that he could not teach this kid and arranged a private tutor. The tutor was Gábor Szegő, who went on to chair the math department at Stanford. Szegő is said to have come away from the first lessons in tears at what the boy could already do. The results of this tutelage showed up a couple years later. At seventeen Johnny gave a new definition of the ordinal numbers, where each number simply is the set of all the numbers before it. Zero is the empty set. One is the set containing zero. Two is the set containing zero and one. And so on up into the infinite ordinals, with nothing but the empty set and a pair of braces to build from. If you think about it, this is a very computer-science-y way to define numbers: an inductive datatype with one constructor.

He pushed this further in his doctoral thesis a few years later. Set theory at the time was still suffering from the paradoxes, Russell's set of all sets that do not contain themselves being the famous one. Johnny's fix was essentially a type system for sets: the ordinary ones you can put inside other sets, and the oversized ones you can talk about but never use as an element. The paradox then becomes a type error. Note that it is the same abstraction move in both times: take an object everyone thinks they understand, and replace it with the smallest thing that behaves the same way.

Johnny kept doing the same thing in field after field for the next thirty years: arrive, find the smallest set of objects and axioms the mess is actually about, write them down so that everyone can finally argue about the right thing, and then leave before the theorems fell out. Teller said Johnny enjoyed thinking, but I think the addiction was much more specialized than that. His real superpower was " the art of abstraction ".

Look at the list from the introduction again with this in mind. Matrix mechanics and wave mechanics looked like rival theories until he noticed they were two coordinate systems on the same Hilbert space. Economists thought comparing preferences across people was hopeless until he asked what minimal consistency axioms a chooser has to satisfy, and derived a cardinal utility scale from them in an afternoon. Self-reproduction looked like it needed an infinite recursion of blueprints until he separated "read the tape as instructions" from "copy the tape as data."

Having finished his PhD at 21, Johnny arrived at Göttingen at 22 because it was the world capital of mathematics, under Hilbert. The timing couldn't have been better. Heisenberg, one year older, was down the hall having just invented matrix mechanics. A year later Schrödinger produced wave mechanics in Vienna. The two gave the same answers and implied completely different pictures of reality, and physicists were uneasy with both: matrices were unfamiliar mathematics then, and nobody could say what the waves were. Von Neumann's first move was to prove the two were the same theory in different forms. Then he wrote "Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics" (1932), which set the whole thing up rigorously in Hilbert space. The author of the book Bhattacharya, who did physics as an undergrad, points out that this is still the most watertight formulation we have.

Once the math was clean, the measurement problem became more visible. Where does the wave function actually collapse? At the apparatus, the detector, the retina, or the conscious observer? Von Neumann declined to take a position, but proved it does not matter mathematically where you draw the line because the answer comes out the same. That line is now called the von Neumann cut.

Nothing much came of game theory until von Neumann proved the minimax theorem in 1928, in his early twenties. Every two-player zero-sum game has a solution: either a strategy one player can pursue to win, or a mixed strategy with randomness in it (e.g., rock-paper-scissors). Then he lost interest and wandered off, as was his habit.

He came back when Oskar Morgenstern turned up at Princeton. Morgenstern, an economist, was stuck on what is essentially a liveness bug in economic modeling: you intervene in an economy, people adjust their behavior in response, which invalidates the model you used to design the intervention, so you build a new model, which they also adjust to. An infinite loop. Morgenstern had concluded that all attempts to model economies must fail, which made him unpopular right up until the Wall Street crash made him look prescient. Von Neumann had the tools to attack the problem. Over about eighteen months they produced the 600-page "Theory of Games and Economic Behavior" (1944) and founded the field. Johnny did this as a hobby. During those same years he was designing implosion lenses at Los Alamos and building the first programmable computers. He would drop in on Morgenstern for a long session and then vanish back into the rest of his life.

items.title: Trovato morto il nipote 29enne di Ranieri III. L’annuncio del Principe Alberto di Monaco
items.summary: Antoine de Massy era uscito di casa sabato sera e da allora non era più tornato. La famiglia ne aveva denunciato la scomparsa
items.content:
Sognava un futuro nel tennis, Antoine de Massy, ​​cugino di secondo grado del Principe Alberto II, 29 anni. Invece, a poche ore dalla sua scomparsa, la conferma: l’uomo è morto e il suo corpo – secondo quanto riporta Monaco-Matin - è stato ritrovato domenica 25 ottobre in un giardino dietro Villa Sauber, vicino al Boulevard du Larvotto. I familiari si erano allarmati perché Antoine non si era presentato a un pranzo in famiglia senza dare spiegazioni, risultando irrintracciabile.

Il procuratore generale di Monaco conferma l’apertura di un' indagine per stabilire le cause del decesso e sembra che ci sia un fermo : nel mattino di lunedì 26 ottobre, una persona è stata fermata dalla polizia, perché in base alle immagini delle telecamere di sorveglianza potrebbe essere considerata un testimone.

È il Palazzo del Principe a dare la notizia della morte di Antonie, pubblicamente, lunedì 26 ottobre, con un comunicato a firma del Principe Alberto II e di sua moglie, la Principessa Charlène : «Le Loro Altezze partecipano al dolore della sua famiglia e dei suoi cari ed esprimono le loro sincere condoglianze in questo momento di dolore». E aggiungono: «Appassionato di tennis, era parte di una storia familiare profondamente connessa a questa disciplina nel Principato».

Visualizza questo post su Instagram Un post condiviso da Antoine De Massy (@antoinedemassy)

Ventinove anni, Antoine de Massy era f iglio di Christian de Massy, ​​cugino primo del Principe Alberto II, e nipote della Principessa Antoinette , sorella maggiore del Principe Ranieri III e quindi zia dell'attuale sovrano del Principato di Monaco. Appassionato di tennis, aveva iniziato a giocare fin da bambino, all’età di 3 anni; nel 2012, in un'intervista a L'Uomo Vogue , aveva raccontato che era stato suo padre ad avvicinarlo allo sport. Si era anche trasferito da Monaco in Florida per seguire un allenamento intensivo parallelamente agli studi, esprimendo la sua ammirazione per Novak Djokovic e aveva espresso il desiderio di rappresentare Monaco ai Giochi Olimpici, un giorno.
